result.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens, when credential sharing is enabled it returns the raw fetch Response from the sync endpoint (no .json() call, no webhook secret header sent either). Google's CalendarService does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` then `const token = res?.data; token.access_token = ...`. A fetch Response has no `data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError inside the try block, so the credential update never runs and the error handling path triggers on every refresh when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true. The mechanism is fully verifia

judged_text: With credential sharing enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response of the sync endpoint, and `res?.data` on a fetch Response is undefined, so `token.access_token` on the next line throws a TypeError. Every Google Calendar token refresh on a sharing-enabled deployment throws inside the try block and never persists new tokens, so calendar operations fall back to the expired access token and start returning 401s — the flagship integration of this sync feature is broken in its own happy path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. In Google Calendar refresh (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), the code then does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`, but a `fetch` Response has no `.data` field (and the body is never `await res.json()`). This makes `token` undefined and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime on sharing-enabled deployments, preventing token persistence.
